post_title: Export clo Pattern shapes to Photoshop for decal and color edits
post_details: I know graphic 3d pattern images can be imported to change pattern color/print details in clo. Is there a way to export the exact pattern shapes into Photoshop so they can be edited and colored? Thank you for your help!!!!

comments.comment_body: Photoshop has long been 'understand' 3d. You can export clothes as a obj and color it in Photoshop. It is much better to use Substance painter of course for these purposes. Adoby bought Painter from allegorhythmic. Now this is the same adobe.

The Print Layout 2D Snapshot will show you a perfect view on painting the 2D flats in the traditional 2D UV style. You can do a lot of detailed coloring and texturing within Clo but if you need more advanced coloring and texturing for use in other programs a dedicated program as Vad mentioned is the best bet. Adobe Substance Painter (as of Jan 2019) or Foundry Mari are each dedicated to painting UV maps in 3D space. Substance Painter is highly capable, cheaper ($239) and is easier to learn. The price may become moot as Adobe rolls it into their creative cloud tool set (eventually). Mari ($599 or free for reduced non-commercial license) is a bit more complicated but it scales and excels for creating very high resolution textures on large assets with lots of udims. Which basically means unless you are creating for film it might be overkill. Try them both and decide which you like better for your needs. Both individual commercial versions have a fully featured 30-day trial available. https://www.substance3d.com/products/substance-painter https://www.foundry.com/products/mari

post_title: HOW TO : Measure a Pattern in 2D
post_details: Hi all, This post will help you to check your pattern spec in 2D. Step 1: Select your Internal Polygon/Line Tool Step 2: Click on the point you want to measure from Step 3: Hold shift to lock the vertical axis, and double click on the bottom of the pattern - this will create an internal line on the pattern. Repeat this step on all measurements you'd like to mark. Step 4: Select the Edit Pattern Tool Step 5: Click on the line. You'll see a couple of measurements: The measurement of the line itself will pop up adjacent to the segment when it's selected The SUM of all the lines selected (if you have multiple) will be show in blue attached to your cursor In the Property Editor - under Selected Line, you'll see: - The Measurement in 2D - The Symmetric measurement (if you're working on symmetrically linked patterns) - The Measurement when the garment is actually draped in 3D - The Symmetric Measurement in 3D Thanks &amp Happy CLOing!

comments.comment_body: Hi 419273818373. When using your POM tool just click once to start at your right hps, then move your mouse over to your left hps and double click to end. The measurement will be there above the yellow line that appears.

Did you suggest anything which can be protect my original texture

comments.comment_body: I actually do not see anything bad with the render. It does look a little flat and without detail which I'll give some suggestions below on how to remedy the flatness. Denim has that really random texture based on how it was woven together. If you are needing a more detailed texture other than the image/color map you might need to add a normal map into the mix. Normal maps give the illusion of depth on the texture based on the angle and distance of the 3D camera. The Clo Manual explains how to apply a normal map. https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000447607-Fabric-Texture-Normal-Map I would suggest for the easiest way to create the necessary texture maps to use Substance Designer https://www.allegorithmic.com/products/substance-designer as it helps you get excellent texture maps for physically based rendering to make your virtual cloth look as real as possible. It all starts at getting the best possible scan/photo of your fabric. If you are not able to get the required quality in your original scan you could use a digital camera or modern smartphone in combination with Substance Designer. Here is a tutorial on how to build a fabric texture from a smartphone photo: https://www.allegorithmic.com/blog/your-smartphone-material-scanner If you need something higher quality fabric scanners are expensive for one off scans. I would suggest https://www.muravision.com/ if you are located in the United States or https://www.vizoo3d.com/services if in Europe as they will scan your fabric samples. Mura doesn't list their cost as they quote based on your individual requirements but Vizoo does. I personally wouldn't do this option unless it is the last resort.

The Library panel being too wide you can move the panel to the size of your liking by dragging the edge. I believe this occurs as Clo will auto scale for the resolution of the monitor. The Font setting it can be changed in the UI settings dialog. https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001547128-User-Interface However if the Clo UI settings do not solve all the issues you might need to change the scale in your OS properties to be able to view applications and text better on high resolution displays.. Sorry I totally misread the original post. I do agree the library panel does seem to have a fixed minimum width. I think the minimum should be just a bit wider than 2 or 3 icons. That way it isn't too small that causes the feeling of infinite scrolling but wide enough that it doesn't get in the way when you want to have it open. I didn't mean change the resolution of the display to accommodate Clo. I meant to change the scaling to something over 100%. On High resolution displays the font and icons will appear to become smaller as the resolution increases. For example the icons and font on a display with 1920x1200 are the same size on a display that is 3840x2160 but they just appear smaller. The scaling feature in the OS display settings scales the icons and text on screen to accommodate for the higher resolution. So 125% scaling increases the icon and text 25% beyond 100% so it is easier for humans to see and read. If an application doesn't override the OS in the GUI then the application text will fluidly change based on the OS scaling setting. I suspect I know what is causing the roll over bug. When "Support for high resolution display" is enabled it is doing a dynamic scaling from within Clo. But when the roll over occurs on the text for whatever reason it is causing the feature to be disabled and the text defaults to the normal size based on the OS scaling setting which makes the text appear really small. I did a Google search on this problem and it appears Adobe has been having this issue for 5K displays as well. In their forums for Windows they suggested turning off the high resolution setting in the application (back to normal 100%) close the application. Then in Windows explorer navigate to the application file and right click on the application and go to Properties &gt Compatibility &gt Change high DPI Settings &gt Override high DPI scaling behavior &gt System Enhanced. You might have to play with the settings to get it to display correctly until Clo fixes the bug.
